name: @diy-accounting-uk/diya-submit

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Sign in to DIY Accounting Submit as the MCP's own Cognito app client: opens the pool's hosted UI in the operator's browser (or prints the URL, when it cannot open one) with a PKCE code challenge, catches the authorization code on a loopback listener, and stores the refresh token under ~/.config/diya-submit/credentials.json mode 600. Every tool that reaches the deployed API (the VAT, Companies House, practice and cloud-book tools) uses the resulting session; run this once before any of them, and again after a sign_out or once the stored refresh token has expired.

tools.name: sign_out
tools.description: Ends the MCP's own session: revokes the refresh token at Cognito, tells DIY Accounting Submit's sign-out route to close it server-side too, then deletes the local credentials file. Best-effort on both network calls, so it still clears the local session when offline or the token is already expired.

tools.name: open_book
tools.description: Open a diya-gl book from the filesystem: a directory holding book.toml and lines.jsonl, or a single file (a DIY Accounting workbook, a package zip, a diya-gl zip, or a diya-gl JSON file). With cloud: true, opens bookId from the DIYA cloud instead (a practice client's own book with clientId), signed in as the session's credentials idToken(). Answers the product, the entity, the period covered, the line count and the book checks summary. Replaces the session's loaded book.

path.description: Path to the book: a directory of book.toml + lines.jsonl, or one file the engine reads; unused with cloud

cloud.description: Open bookId from the DIYA cloud instead of the filesystem

bookId.description: The cloud book's id; required with cloud: true

clientId.description: A practice client's id, to open that client's book instead of the practice's own

tools.name: list_books
tools.description: List the books saved in the DIYA cloud, most recently updated first, signed in as the session's credentials. Each row carries the bookId open_book takes. With clientId, lists that practice client's books instead of the practice's own.

clientId.description: A practice client's id, to list that client's books instead of the practice's own

tools.name: save_book
tools.description: Save the session's loaded book to the filesystem. Formats: diya-gl-dir (book.toml + lines.jsonl into a directory; the default for a path with no extension), diya-gl-zip, json, xlsx (the product's recalculating workbook) and zip (the product's package). xlsx and zip fetch the template from spreadsheets.diyaccounting.co.uk on first use. With cloud: true, writes to the DIYA cloud by bookId instead (a practice client's book set with clientId), signed in as the session's credentials; carries the if-match etag from the session's last cloud open or save of the same bookId.

path.description: Where to write: a directory for diya-gl-dir, otherwise a file path; unused with cloud

format.description: One of diya-gl-dir, diya-gl-zip, json, xlsx, zip; unused with cloud

cloud.description: Save to the DIYA cloud by bookId instead of the filesystem

bookId.description: The cloud book's id; required with cloud: true

clientId.description: A practice client's id, to save into that client's book set

tools.name: write_finance_package
tools.description: Writes a diya-gl book and its lines as the unzipped spreadsheets package directory a completed year's package holds: one workbook for a single-file product (Basic Sole Trader, Taxi Driver), the whole named set for a multi-file one (Self Employed, Company), under outputDir in a directory named the product's own way. Reads the book from bookPath (a diya-gl-dir, or any file open_book reads) or from book and lines given directly; does not touch the session's own loaded book. Reads the workbook templates from templatePackagePath (the spreadsheets repository's app/ directory) when given, otherwise fetches them from spreadsheets.diyaccounting.co.uk on first use.

bookPath.description: Path to the book: a directory of book.toml + lines.jsonl, or one file the engine reads

book.description: A parsed book.toml, instead of bookPath

lines.description: Parsed lines.jsonl entries, instead of bookPath

templatePackagePath.description: The spreadsheets repository's app/ directory, read directly instead of fetching templates over the network

outputDir.description: The directory the package's own named directory is written under

tools.name: derive_vat_return
tools.description: The nine VAT boxes for one obligation period from the session's loaded book, read from the engine's own VAT interface: the quarter ending on periodEnd (a month end the book carries), with HMRC's field names and rounding, the three months' figures, and every sales and purchases journal line that fed boxes 1, 4, 6 and 7. Refuses a book that is not VAT registered, a period the book does not carry, and a period whose lines do not reconcile with the interface.

periodEnd.description: The obligation's period end, YYYY-MM-DD; must be a month end the book's VAT interface carries

periodStart.description: The obligation's period start, YYYY-MM-DD; refused unless it opens the quarter ending periodEnd

periodKey.description: The obligation's period key, echoed back for the submit call

tools.name: prepare_vat_return
tools.description: Derives the VAT return for the quarter ending on periodEnd from the session's loaded book, exactly as derive_vat_return does, and answers a link to the VAT form on the Submit site with the seven figures filled in (the form works out boxes 3 and 5 itself). This tool never files anything and reaches no outside service. The person opens the link, checks the figures on the page, ticks the declaration and files there; the figures filed are the figures the page shows. Show the person the figures this tool answers, give them the link, and tell them to check, declare and file on the page.

periodEnd.description: The obligation's period end, YYYY-MM-DD; must be a month end the book's VAT interface carries

periodStart.description: The obligation's period start, YYYY-MM-DD; refused unless it opens the quarter ending periodEnd

tools.name: derive_micro_entity_accounts
tools.description: The seven FRS 105 balance-sheet lines the accounts filing takes, from the session's loaded book: the current year from the engine's published balance sheet and the prior year from the book's opening balance, in whole pounds with capital and reserves equal to net assets, plus the period dates, the company number and name, the first director and the employee count. Refuses a book whose published or opening balance sheet does not balance.

tools.name: derive_small_company_accounts
tools.description: The figures a small company's FRS 102 section 1A accounts filing takes, from the session's loaded book: the full profit and loss account and the balance sheet sub-lines for the current year from the engine's published statements, the prior-year balance sheet from the opening balance, the tangible fixed asset note by class, the period dates, the company number and name, the directors and the employee count, in whole pounds with every subtotal holding. The book publishes no prior-year profit and loss account, so none is returned. Refuses a book whose published or opening balance sheet does not balance.

tools.name: derive_company_tax_return
tools.description: The figures the Company Tax Return form takes, from the session's loaded Company book: the accounting period, the computation figures (depreciation, amortisation, entertaining, capital allowances, franked investment income, losses brought forward), the profit and loss account from the engine's published statements, and the book's own trading profit and Corporation Tax as a working sheet for a check. Refuses a book that is not a Company book, makes a trading loss or carries net non-trading loan relationship debits. With a path, also writes the answer as the JSON file the Company Tax Return page's "Fill from your books" card reads.

path.description: Where to write the answer as JSON for the Company Tax Return page's import

tools.name: request_hmrc_authorisation
tools.description: Answers HMRC's sign-in link for this session, so the VAT tools can call HMRC without a token in the chat. Answers {url, expiresAt, scope, hmrcAccount}: show the user the url, wait for them to say HMRC access is granted, then call list_vat_obligations or submit_vat_return. The link works once, for ten minutes. DIY Accounting Submit keeps HMRC's tokens itself and renews the access token for the rest of the session. A second call replaces the session's authorisation. hmrcAccount synthetic is HMRC's sandbox. Over the deployed API.

services.description: The HMRC services to ask access for: vat (the default), itsa, and agent (the practice tools invite_client and client_authorisation_status)

hmrcAccount.description: Which HMRC environment: live (the default) or synthetic

tools.name: list_vat_obligations

clientId.description: A practice client's id, to resolve vrn from the client row instead

from.description: From date, YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to the start of the current calendar year

to.description: To date, YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

status.description: O (Open) or F (Fulfilled); both when omitted

hmrcAccount.description: Which HMRC environment to call; defaults to the session's HMRC authorisation's own

tools.name: list_vat_liabilities
tools.description: What HMRC says the business owes for VAT, by period, for one VRN over the deployed API. Uses the session's HMRC authorisation: call request_hmrc_authorisation first if this tool says none is held.

to.description: To date, YYYY-MM-DD; HMRC's default range when omitted

hmrcAccount.description: Which HMRC environment to call; defaults to the session's HMRC authorisation's own

tools.name: request_companies_house_codes
tools.description: Answers a link where the user types the Companies House codes a filing needs, so the codes never appear in the chat. Answers {entryId, url, expiresAt}: show the user the url, wait for them to say they have saved the codes, then pass entryId as codesEntryId to the filing tool. The link works for ten minutes. A single entry is used up by one filing call; ask again for a second filing. To file for several practice clients through run_for_clients, give clientIds (kind accounts or confirmation-statement-data, no companyNumber): the page then asks for one company authentication code per client by name, and each client's filing call takes only its own client's codes, so the one entryId serves the whole batch. kind accounts is for submit_micro_entity_accounts_sandbox and submit_small_company_accounts_sandbox, confirmation-statement-data for get_confirmation_statement_data_sandbox, and confirmation-statement (with directors, in the order the filing lists them) for submit_confirmation_statement_sandbox. Over the deployed API.

companyNumber.description: The 8-character Companies House company number; required unless clientIds is given

directors.description: Confirmation statement only: the directors in filing order; the page asks for one personal code each

The company authentication code is not an argument: the user types it on the link request_companies_house_codes (kind confirmation-statement-data) answers, and this call names that entry by codesEntryId, which it uses up.

Calls DIY Accounting Submit's own move route, which copies the book and every kept version, verifies each copy, then deletes the source. Refuses when the client already has a book with this id, or the practice has no such book of its own.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: The signed-in practice's own client list over the deployed API: each client's id, display name, identifiers (VRN, NINO, UTR, company number) and current HMRC authorisation state per service. Archived clients are excluded.

tools.name: add_client
tools.description: Adds one client to the practice's list, over the deployed API. Every identifier is optional, but a given one must match its HMRC or Companies House format.

tools.name: invite_client
tools.description: Sends an HMRC Agent Authorisation invitation for one client and one service, over the deployed API. The client's own VRN or NINO comes from the client row, not from this call. Uses the session's HMRC authorisation: call request_hmrc_authorisation with services agent first if this tool says none is held.

tools.name: client_authorisation_status

tools.name: run_for_clients
tools.description: Runs one client-scoped tool once per client in the practice's own list (list_clients), passing each client's clientId in turn. Returns one row per client -- {clientId, displayName, ok, result or error} -- plus a summary count; one client's failure never stops the rest. tool is one of list_vat_obligations, submit_vat_return, get_vat_receipt, submit_micro_entity_accounts_sandbox, submit_small_company_accounts_sandbox, open_book, save_book. For the two accounts tools, put in args a codesEntryId that request_companies_house_codes answered for these clients' clientIds; each client's call takes its own codes from it.

tool.description: The client-scoped tool to run for every client

args.description: That tool's other arguments; clientId is added per client and overrides any given here

tools.name: derive_itsa_quarterly_update
tools.description: One period of HMRC's Self Employment Business API from the loaded self-employed book: the period's own figures in a tax year filed as dated period summaries, a running total from 6 April in a year filed as cumulative period summaries (2025-26 on). Picks the period by periodEndDate among the year's four (standard quarters by default); with no periodEndDate answers every period. A field the book cannot source is omitted, never sent as zero.

periodEndDate.description: The period's end date, YYYY-MM-DD, as HMRC's obligation names it

quarterlyPeriodType.description: standard (6 April quarters, the default) or calendar

taxYear.description: Override the tax year the book's dates imply, as 2025-26

tools.name: derive_itsa_annual_submission
tools.description: The year's allowances and adjustments for HMRC's Self Employment Business API annual submission from the loaded self-employed book, restricted to the fields HMRC accepts for that tax year. With a path, also writes the answer as the JSON file hmrc/itsa/annualSubmission.html imports.

taxYear.description: Override the tax year the book's dates imply, as 2025-26

path.description: Where to write the answer as JSON for the annual submission page's import

tools.name: derive_uk_property_period
tools.description: One period of HMRC's UK property income and expenses from the loaded landlord book whose chart names the property accounts: the period's own figures, both ends inclusive; a cumulative year's running total is the same call with the period starting on 6 April. Answers the income, the expenses, the slots the book did not fill and the postings behind each figure. Refuses a period carrying both consolidated and itemised expenses.

tools.name: derive_uk_property_annual
tools.description: The year's adjustments and allowances for HMRC's UK property annual submission from the loaded landlord book whose chart names the property accounts. The elections and the landlord facts are left to the annual submission page and named in leftToPage.

tools.name: submit_itsa_quarterly_update
tools.description: Files one period of HMRC's Self Employment Business API (derive_itsa_quarterly_update's figures, once the user has confirmed them) over the deployed API. In a tax year filed as cumulative period summaries (2025-26 on) the figures are the running total from 6 April and the period dates are optional; in earlier years they are required. Uses the session's HMRC authorisation for the itsa service: call request_hmrc_authorisation with services ["itsa"] first if this tool says none is held.

businessId.description: The self-employment business id HMRC holds, for example XAIS12345678901

periodIncome.description: Income by field, as derive_itsa_quarterly_update answers it

periodExpenses.description: Expenses by field, as derive_itsa_quarterly_update answers it

periodDisallowableExpenses.description: Disallowable expenses by field, as derive_itsa_quarterly_update answers it

hmrcAccount.description: Which HMRC environment to call; defaults to the session's HMRC authorisation's own

tools.name: submit_itsa_annual_submission
tools.description: Files the year's allowances and adjustments for HMRC's Self Employment Business API annual submission (derive_itsa_annual_submission's figures, once the user has confirmed them) over the deployed API. Uses the session's HMRC authorisation for the itsa service: call request_hmrc_authorisation with services ["itsa"] first if this tool says none is held.

businessId.description: The self-employment business id HMRC holds, for example XAIS12345678901

adjustments.description: Adjustments by field, as derive_itsa_annual_submission answers them

allowances.description: Allowances by field, as derive_itsa_annual_submission answers them

nonFinancials.description: The non-financial facts HMRC takes, when the year needs them

hmrcAccount.description: Which HMRC environment to call; defaults to the session's HMRC authorisation's own
